subject: Acme performance SLO/SLA follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme performance SLO/SLA follow-up

Hi Jordan 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on performance expectations and the SLA language:

Recap
- Target workloads: low-latency chat API for customer-facing product search (avg request size ~150 tokens, typical context 1024 tokens).
- Primary SLOs discussed: p95 inference latency target of 120ms (time-to-first-byte) for standard responses under steady-state traffic; sustained throughput target of ~150 requests/sec for this tenant at peak.
- Streaming: we agreed time-to-first-token is critical for perceived latency; streaming model will require measuring time-to-first-token (TTFT) and token emission rate for long responses.
- Concurrency: Acme expects concurrent request bursts up to 300 concurrent requests; you asked about burst handling vs. queued concurrency slots.

Action items / next steps
1) I'll attach a draft SLA and our proposed measurement definitions (attached: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf). Please review and flag any hard stops.
2) Connor / Ethan: can you provide model-specific throughput / concurrency guidance and how we measure streaming TTFT?
3) Jordan: can you confirm whether the 300 concurrent requests is peak-per-region or global? Also confirm if the 120ms p95 target is acceptable as a preliminary objective.

High-level ask: if we can agree on measurement definitions and a concise exclusion list (maintenance windows, force majeure, customer-side network), we can convert this into a trial SLA for the pilot and surface drafting to legal.

Thanks 
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf, telemetry-schema.csv

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@acme.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme performance SLO/SLA follow-up

Marissa 

Thanks for the summary and the draft. A few clarifying questions from our side before we loop in procurement/legal:

1) Measurement window and vantage: when you say p95 inference latency (120ms), where is that measured from/to? Is it measured at Redwood ingress (your edge) to last byte sent, or does that include our network egress to our region? We need clarity because our monitoring measures from our app server to your API gateway.

2) Streaming semantics: for long responses we care about: (a) time-to-first-token, (b) median token emission rate after the first token, and (c) whether you count partial failures (mid-stream disconnects) as SLA violations.

3) Concurrency vs. throttling: if we hit 300 concurrent requests, do you queue requests (with expected queue latency) or do you reject/return 429s? What's the burst handling policy and how will that appear from our side?

4) Exclusions / maintenance: acceptable to have scheduled maintenance exclude SLA measurements, but we need to see the standard notice period (48h?), and also want to see a clear list of exclusions (e.g., third-party outages, customer-side network issues, DDOS).

5) Remedies / credits: what's the proposed service credit structure for missed SLOs? A simple formula would be helpful (e.g., X% of monthly bill per SLO breach bucket).

We can loop in procurement once we have concrete definitions for measurement and remedies. Also happy to set a short technical sync with your SEs to walk telemetry and test plans.

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme performance SLO/SLA follow-up

Jordan 

Appreciate the questions. Quick technical clarifications to address each point; happy to do a short demo of telemetry next week if helpful.

1) Measurement definition- We measure latency from the moment the request is accepted by Redwood's ingress load balancer (timestamp T0) to the time the final byte of the response is emitted from our platform (timestamp T_end). For streaming, we record two primary metrics: time-to-first-token (TTFT = T_first - T0) and total end-to-end duration (T_end - T0). All SLA pX numbers in the draft are computed on the pX percentile of the corresponding metric measured at our ingress.

Notes on network: That measurement excludes downstream network transit after our egress. If you prefer measurement from your app server, we can provide telemetry hooks and a small script to correlate your client side timings with our ingress timings for joint reporting.

2) Streaming behavior- Partial stream disconnects: by default we do not treat transient client disconnects as platform failures unless the disconnect is demonstrably caused by an internal service error (5xx). We log and report mid-stream 5xx events and they are eligible for SLA consideration. For long responses we provide TTFT and token emission rate metrics (tokens/sec) and can include median and p95 rates in monthly reports.

3) Concurrency / throttling- For dedicated tenants we expose a configurable concurrency limit. When concurrency is exceeded we can be configured to either queue (with a soft queue latency target) or return 429s. For the pilot we recommend queueing with a max queue latency of 250ms and then failing with 429s beyond that. Concrete behaviour will depend on the Dedicated capacity plan you select.

4) Maintenance & exclusions- Standard scheduled maintenance with >=48h notice is excluded. Other exclusions we typically include: customer-side network failures, third-party provider outages (CDN/cloud incidents), force majeure, and actions taken at customer's direction (e.g., custom model changes). We can enumerate these in the SLA.

5) Remedies / credits- Our standard proposal (see attached draft) is tiered credits: 5% credit for missing monthly p95 targets once, up to 10% for repeated breaches within the same billing period. We can make this sliding or cap at a maximum (e.g., 15%). Legal/procurement may propose edits; the numbers are negotiable for enterprise agreements.

Attachments included: telemetry-schema.csv (sample metrics / event keys you can ingest).

If helpful I can include sample Grafana dashboard queries and a short runbook for correlating your client-side traces with our ingress logs. Shall I schedule a 30-min sync for next Tues/Wed?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme performance SLO/SLA follow-up

Jordan 

Thanks for the great questions and Ethan for the clarifications. To keep momentum, here is a proposed concise SLA paragraph we can put in the pilot agreement; please review and flag any redlines. If we agree in principle, I'll hand this to legal/procurement for formal review.

Proposed SLA paragraph (pilot)- Redwood will measure inference latency from request acceptance at Redwood ingress to last byte emitted from Redwood (ingress-to-egress). For standard (non-streaming) responses, Redwood will target p95 latency <= 120ms. For streaming responses Redwood will target p95 time-to-first-token <= 150ms and maintain a median token emission rate >= 40 tokens/sec for long responses (>500 tokens). Scheduled maintenance with >=48 hours notice, customer-side network issues, third-party provider outages, and force majeure are excluded from SLA calculations. Monthly SLA reporting will be provided in the Redwood Console and a monthly PDF summary sent to platform@acme.com. Remedies for SLA breaches will be service credits applied to the next invoice: 5% credit for a single monthly breach, 10% for two breaches in a month, up to a 15% cap.

Next steps
- Jordan: confirm whether 300 concurrent requests is global or per-region.
- Connor/Ethan: please prepare short telemetry runbook and a sample Grafana dashboard to help Acme correlate client-side timings with our ingress metrics.
- Marissa: I'll open a procurement thread and attach the draft SLA for legal review once we hear back.

Happy to schedule that 30-min technical sync next week 

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
